author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Danish filmmaker May el-Toukhy’s postwar drama “Woman Unknown” won the Golden Lion for best film at the 2026 Venice Film Festival. The film’s lead, Mathilde Arcel, also received the festival’s best actress award, giving the production two of the closing ceremony’s most prominent honors.

Set after World War II, the film follows a Danish housemaid whose past relationship with a German soldier threatens her future and exposes the public punishment faced by women accused of fraternizing with occupying forces. El-Toukhy was the only woman among the 21 directors in the festival’s main competition, a disparity that remained part of the discussion around this year’s lineup.

Other major awards went to Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love,” which received the Silver Lion Grand Jury Prize, and Ilya Khrzhanovsky, who won best director for “DAU.” John Malkovich took best actor for “Wild Horse Nine.” The Golden Lion is closely watched because Venice opens the international awards season and often provides an early platform for films and performances that later contend for major prizes. “Woman Unknown” leaves the festival with both its top film award and recognition for its central performance.
dek: May el-Toukhy’s postwar drama took the Golden Lion, while lead performer Mathilde Arcel won best actress.
headline: “Woman Unknown” wins Golden Lion at Venice Film Festival
